review_basis: Independently opened each of the eight candidate PNGs with view_image. No other PNG or independent reference image was opened.
Read the input manifest and the relevant case sidecar identity, state, checks, intentional differences, and evidence hashes.
Compared the actual PNG SHA-256 values with both expected_png_sha256 and each case sidecar screenshot evidence hash; all eight match.

Used phase3-reference-scope.json, phase3-prototype-reference-support.json, DESIGN_HANDOFF.md, authoritative HANDOFF.md section 5.5, and the static sc-search.dc.html/sc-browse.dc.html declarations as textual review criteria. The prototype was not executed.

observations: The portrait result screen retains the fixture query and the single Local Komga fixture scope. Its summary reports one searched source and zero sources with results.
The named source row explicitly shows the no-results state, without book tiles or a retry action. This agrees with count=0, pending=false, error=false, and busy=false in the captured state.
The five-destination dock is restored with Search active. The query field and scope controls have white outlined surfaces, and no UI shadow, dimmed backdrop, or stippled UI fill is visible.

Local Komga fixture remains identifiable and shows an operation-not-completed status with a separate right-aligned Retry action. The screenshot does not present the failure as successful or as an ordinary no-results response.
The state records a non-timeout error with zero results, pending=false, and busy=false. The absence of book tiles and loading indicators agrees with that settled failure state.
The query, source scopes, summary, and active Search dock remain visible without overlap or a keyboard covering the result area.

The recovered source group displays a count of 20 and six cover tiles with title and author/chapter metadata, matching the Scribe six-cover group allocation. View all is visible at the right of the group heading.
The failure/retrying labels have been replaced by records, consistent with count=20, pending=false, error=false, and busy=false in the captured state.

The Search dock is restored. The fixture titles are deliberately ellipsized within their columns rather than overlapping adjacent tiles; differences from the handoff's sample titles and covers are data differences.

This PNG was opened separately even though its hash equals the success capture. The matching appearance is consistent with both cases ending in the same recorded result state; it alone does not establish that the retry request occurred.
The named source row and its action both visibly say that retry is in progress. No successful result count or book tiles are fabricated while the request is pending.
The summary reports zero completed sources and zero sources with results. This agrees with pending=true, busy=true, and the case's intentional_inflight_capture=true metadata.
A compact, white, black-outlined reading-status toast appears above the dock without dimming the page. The query, scope controls, and active Search dock remain in place.
The summary reports one searched source and one source with results. Local Komga fixture shows 20 results, six cover/title/metadata tiles, and a visible View all action.

The displayed records agree with the captured successful source state: pending=false, error=false, search_result_count=20, and busy=false. The white and gray fixture cover artwork is treated as actual record imagery rather than a UI background treatment.
The six-column search group fits within the 36-pixel page margins, and the restored dock highlights Search. No loading toast, error status, or keyboard obscures the settled results.
The connected source opens a populated catalog with five columns and three rows of actual fixture records. Titles and serial/completed chapter states appear below the cover artwork.

The source heading, source switch, catalog tabs, search field, and filter control remain visible above the grid. The folio displays page 1 of 3 with a Next action, and Browse is active in the retained Scribe dock.

The visible catalog agrees with route=catalog, source_needs_setup=false, the recorded connected status, catalog_result_count=20, and busy=false. Connection setup fields do not obscure the available records in this case.

After View all, the screenshot shows the source's server address, a masked credential field, phone-entry and Test and connect actions, and a not-yet-verified connection status. It shows neither result cards nor a result folio.

The sidecar records route=catalog, busy=false, catalog_count=40, catalog_result_count=40, and ten visible_catalog records titled Local fixture series 030 through 039. It also records source_needs_setup=true and the not-yet-verified status. The rendered setup gate therefore hides nonempty, already obtained catalog results.

The configured source identity and Browse dock are retained, and the form itself uses white outlined fields. The confirmed problem is the result flow's visible state conflict, not a missing or blank screenshot.
The separate server-connect capture demonstrates a recoverable path to a populated catalog. These static artifacts do not establish the implementation cause of the View all gating conflict.
Local Komga fixture explicitly reports Request timed out and exposes a right-aligned Retry action. This remains distinguishable from the empty response and from retry in progress.

The summary reports one searched source and zero sources with results. The absence of cards or a continuing loading indicator agrees with timeout=true, error=true, pending=false, and busy=false in the captured state.
The original query and scope controls remain intact, and the active Search dock is restored without a keyboard or overlay covering the recovery action.

suggestions.description: View all hides available catalog results behind the server connection setup form.
evidence: The actual candidate PNG displays the server configuration fields and not-yet-verified connection status, with no catalog cards or folio.

The matching sidecar records route=catalog, busy=false, catalog_count=40, catalog_result_count=40, and visible_catalog containing the ten real records Local fixture series 030 through 039, while source_needs_setup=true.

The producer's View-all opens real source results check passes on catalog state, but the manually viewed PNG does not present those results. Static sc-search.dc.html line 95 links View all to the source catalog, and the approved scope requires real, source-grouped result navigation.

The server-connect case in this batch does show a populated five-by-three catalog, so the evidence supports a recoverable View all flow defect rather than a global inability to render catalogs. The underlying implementation cause remains undetermined.
suggestions.recommendation: Reconcile the source setup gate with the real fetched catalog state when entering from View all. Present the obtained catalog records and their folio, or show a specific, truthful reason that actually prevents using them with a clear recovery action. Do not require the user to repeat connection setup merely to expose records already available to this settled route, and do not fabricate a verified connection status.

coverage_gaps: All search captures contain one HTTP source group. Simultaneous mixed success, empty, pending, and failure groups are not present, so cross-source nonblocking behavior is not established by this batch.

No independent reference PNG was supplied or viewed. Geometry and state expectations were checked against the approved scope and static handoff/prototype text rather than an export-to-candidate pixel comparison.
This batch does not show search keyboard editing, a content-height sheet, tracking authorization, or absent-hardware controls. Those surfaces and their interactions are outside these eight captures.
limitations: Only the assigned existing PNGs and relevant JSON/text were read, and current PNG hashes were computed. No application, prototype, build, test, validation suite, smoke test, or runtime probe was executed locally or remotely for this review.

Producer check pass flags and reported HTTP request provenance are supporting capture evidence, not substitutes for the independent visual observations. The View all defect remains despite its mechanical checks passing.

Static screenshots do not prove retry activation semantics, request ordering, refresh timing, pagination interaction, persistence, or endpoint operation. Case sidecars identify the recorded phases but were not regenerated.
No conclusion about physical Kindle wake restoration, hardware qualification, or a 512 MiB memory limit is drawn from these desktop-backend PNGs.
This result covers only supplemental-27 for the identified frozen Candidate 3 round-1 run. It is not a claim that the complete round is clean.
